name: Chest Press Machine
machineIdentification: A seat with a vertical back pad and two handles at chest height that push straight away from you. Often has a foot lever near the floor to bring the handles into reach.
instructions: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Sit back with your shoulders against the pad.
Take both handles with a full grip.
Press forward until your arms are almost straight.
Let the handles come back until you feel a stretch across the chest.
keyCues: Keep your shoulder blades pinned back and down.
Stop just short of locking the elbows.
Control the return — don't let the stack slam.
commonMistakes: Setting the seat too high, which shifts the work to the shoulders.
Letting the shoulders roll forward at the end of each press.
Cutting the return short and never stretching the chest.

name: Incline Chest Press Machine
machineIdentification: Like the chest press, but the back pad is reclined and the handles travel up and away at an angle rather than straight forward.
instructions: Set the seat so the handles sit just below your collarbone.
Sit back firmly against the angled pad.
Grip both handles.
Press up and away until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower under control to a comfortable stretch.
keyCues: Keep your back flat on the pad — don't arch off it.
Press along the angle of the machine, not straight up.
Take two seconds on the way down.
commonMistakes: Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees from the body.
Bouncing at the bottom of each rep.
Going heavier than the shoulders can safely stabilize.

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
machineIdentification: A flat bench and a pair of dumbbells. No fixed machine — you control the path entirely.
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell on each thigh.
Lie back, using your knees to help kick the dumbbells into place.
Start with the dumbbells at chest width, arms extended.
Lower them until your upper arms are level with your torso.
Press back up without clanging them together.
keyCues: Pull your shoulder blades together and keep them there.
Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows.
Plant both feet flat on the floor.
commonMistakes: Dropping the elbows far below the bench and straining the shoulders.
Pressing the dumbbells together and losing chest tension.
Letting one arm drift ahead of the other.

name: Barbell Bench Press
machineIdentification: A flat bench inside a rack with a barbell on the uprights above your chest. Look for safety bars set at chest height.
instructions: Lie back so your eyes are under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Unrack and bring the bar over your chest.
Lower to touch just below your nipples.
Press back up over your chest.
keyCues: Keep your shoulder blades squeezed and your upper back tight.
Tuck the elbows to about 45 degrees, not straight out.
Set the safety bars before you start.
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest.
Flaring the elbows wide, which strains the shoulder joint.
Lifting the hips off the bench to grind out a rep.

name: Pec Deck
machineIdentification: A seat with two tall arms either side that swing together in front of you. You either grip vertical handles or press your forearms into pads.
instructions: Set the seat so the handles are at chest height.
Sit back with your shoulders against the pad.
Take both handles with a slight bend in the elbows.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest.
Open back up slowly until you feel a stretch.
keyCues: Keep the elbow angle fixed — this is a hug, not a press.
Squeeze for a beat when the handles meet.
Keep your shoulders back against the pad.
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows like a press.
Opening so far back that the shoulders take the strain.
Rushing through reps with no pause at the squeeze.

name: Cable Chest Fly
machineIdentification: A twin cable tower with a pulley on each side. Set both pulleys at roughly shoulder height with single D-handles attached.
instructions: Set both pulleys at shoulder height with D-handles.
Take one handle in each hand and step forward into a split stance.
Start with arms open and a slight bend in the elbows.
Bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Open back out slowly to a stretch.
keyCues: Hold the elbow bend constant through the whole rep.
Lean slightly forward into the movement.
Cross your hands slightly at the finish for a bigger squeeze.
commonMistakes: Turning it into a press by straightening the arms.
Standing too far back and losing tension at the finish.
Letting the cables drag the shoulders back at the stretch.

name: Push-up
instructions: Set your hands slightly wider than your shoulders.
Straighten your legs so your body forms one line.
Lower until your chest is a fist's height from the floor.
Press back up to straight arms.
keyCues: Squeeze your glutes so your hips don't sag.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees to your body.
Raise your hands onto a bench to make it easier.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips sag or pike up.
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides.
Dipping the head instead of the chest.
